description:
Welcome to People's Last Hope - home of Project AKARIA.

I’m a robotics engineer passionate about autonomous systems, space exploration, and hardware-software integration. For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, I am tackling the "Flame in Freefall" challenge by developing AKARIA - an autonomous orbital fire-response unit designed to detect and suppress microgravity fires before they threaten the crew.
summary:
Akaria is a web-based dashboard that helps people explore NASA's research on fire and combustion in space. I developed a platform that combines a collection of research data with a search tool connected to NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database.

Users can search for experiments, view their objectives, and explore information about fuels, experimental conditions, and equipment. This makes it easier to find and understand research that would otherwise require searching through many separate records.

Fire behaves differently in space than it does on Earth. Understanding these differences is important for keeping astronauts safe during future missions. Akaria aims to make NASA's existing research easier to access and explore, so that students, researchers, and anyone interested in space exploration can better understand what scientists have already discovered.
details:
Akaria - Project Details

Akaria is a web-based research dashboard designed to make NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to access and explore. It combines a local collection of BASS (Burning and Suppression of Solids) research data with live search capabilities for NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database.

Users can browse available research records, search for investigations by topic, and explore information such as experimental objectives, research areas, conditions, fuels, and hardware when these details are available. By bringing these resources into one interface, Akaria reduces the time and effort needed to find relevant experiments and understand existing research.

The project addresses an important challenge in space exploration: fire behaves differently in microgravity, and understanding combustion under these conditions is essential for improving fire safety aboard spacecraft and in future lunar and Martian habitats. Akaria aims to support students, researchers, and engineers by making existing experimental knowledge more accessible and easier to explore. It does not currently predict fire behavior or provide certified safety recommendations.

Akaria was developed using Python and Streamlit. The project also uses Requests for communication with NASA's PSI database, JSON for structured data storage, and PyMuPDF and Pillow for document and image processing. The development process involved organizing research data, integrating the NASA search interface, and building the dashboard.

The creative aspect of Akaria is its combination of locally organized research data and live NASA database search in a single, accessible platform. Instead of presenting isolated research records, it provides a unified starting point for exploring experiments relevant to combustion in space.

During development, we considered data accessibility, clarity of presentation, the reliability of available sources, and the limitations of the collected research information. Future improvements could include broader dataset integration, side-by-side experiment comparisons, and transparent relevance ranking to help users identify the most relevant studies.
